lessons.title: Area of Regular Polygons
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a regular polygon by decomposing it into triangles.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words regular polygon, decompose, triangle, and composite.

concept.heading: How do we find the area of a regular polygon?
concept.intro: A regular polygon is a closed shape with straight sides where every side is the same length and every angle is the same size. We can decompose it (break it apart) into equal triangles from the center, then add up their areas.
concept.keyIdea: Area of Regular Polygons. Formula: Area = (Number of Sides) × (Area of One Triangle). 1. Decompose the regular polygon from center into n congruent triangles. 2. Find the area of one triangle using A = ½ × side × apothem (height). 3. Multiply by the total number of sides

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My hexagon has 6 equal sides. Each side is 6 feet, and each center triangle has a height of 5.2 feet. Use the rounded height to estimate the area.
First I find one triangle: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
I multiply: 6 × 5.2 = 31.2, then ½ × 31.2 = 15.6 square feet.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it has 6 equal triangles.
I multiply: 6 × 15.6 = 93.6. So the total area is 93.6 square feet.
linesEs: Mi hexágono tiene 6 lados iguales. Cada lado mide 6 pies, y cada triángulo del centro tiene una altura de 5.2 pies. Usa la altura redondeada para estimar el área.
Primero hallo un triángulo: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
Un hexágono tiene 6 lados, así que tiene 6 triángulos iguales.
Multiplico: 6 × 15.6 = 93.6. Entonces el área total es 93.6 pies cuadrados.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller regular pentagon: each of its 5 triangles has base 4 cm and height 3 cm. Use the rounded height to estimate the area.
First find one triangle: ½ × 4 × 3. What is 4 × 3? Yes, 12, and half of 12 is 6 sq cm.
A pentagon has 5 sides, so how many triangles? Yes, 5.
Multiply: 5 × 6 = 30, so the total area is 30 square centimeters.
linesEs: Ahora un pentágono regular más pequeño: cada uno de sus 5 triángulos tiene base 4 cm y altura 3 cm. Usa la altura redondeada para estimar el área.
Primero halla un triángulo: ½ × 4 × 3. ¿Cuánto es 4 × 3? Sí, 12, y la mitad de 12 es 6 cm cuadrados.
Un pentágono tiene 5 lados, entonces ¿cuántos triángulos? Sí, 5.
Multiplica: 5 × 6 = 30, así que el área total es 30 centímetros cuadrados.

vocabulary.definition: The space a regular polygon covers. Split it from the center into identical triangles, find one triangle's area, then multiply by how many there are.
vocabulary.example: A hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles: (½ × 4 × 3.5) × 6 = 42 square units

vocabulary.definition: A closed flat shape made of straight sides, where every side is the same length and every angle is the same size.
vocabulary.example: A stop sign is a regular octagon — all 8 sides are the same length and all 8 angles are equal

vocabulary.definition: To break a shape into smaller, simpler shapes.
vocabulary.example: Draw lines from the center of a hexagon to each corner → you get 6 equal triangles you can find the area of

vocabulary.definition: A shape with three sides.
vocabulary.example: Each triangle inside a decomposed hexagon has a base = one side of the hexagon and height = distance from center to side

vocabulary.definition: Made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.example: 6 triangles, each with area 15 sq ft, combine to form a hexagon with total area = 6 × 15 = 90 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.example: For a regular hexagon: Total Area = 6 × (½ × b × h), where b = side length and h = height of each triangle

lessons.title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
lessons.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism, including ones with fractional edge lengths, using base area × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words volume, rectangular prism, dimensions, and base area.

concept.heading: How do we find volume when an edge is a fraction?
concept.intro: Volume is the space inside a rectangular prism. There are two ways to write the same rule. You can multiply all three edges, V = length × width × height. Or you can find the base area first, B = length × width, and then stack that base up the height: V = B × h. Both give the same number, and both work when an edge is a fraction or a decimal.
concept.keyIdea: Volume of Rectangular Prisms with Fractional Edges. Formula: V = l × w × h = B × h. 1. Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying. 2. Multiply numerators across, multiply denominators across: V = (l · w · h). 3. Simplify the fraction and label with cubic units

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My capsule is 2 ft long, 1.5 ft wide, and 1 ft tall. I write V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1.
So the volume is 3 ft³. A fractional edge like 1.5 did not change my steps at all.
linesEs: Mi cápsula mide 2 pies de largo, 1.5 pies de ancho y 1 pie de alto. Escribo V = largo × ancho × alto.
Entonces el volumen es 3 pies³. Una arista fraccionaria como 1.5 no cambió mis pasos para nada.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now try a box that is 4 long, 2 wide, and 0.5 tall. Let's do it the base-area way. What is the base, 4 × 2?
The base area is B = 8. Picture that base sitting on the table — that is one layer.
Now stack the base up the height: V = B × h = 8 × 0.5 (that means half of 8). What is the volume?
Yes, V = 4 cubic units. Check it the other way: 4 × 2 × 0.5 = 4. Same answer, because B × h already used the length and width.
linesEs: Ahora prueba con una caja de 4 de largo, 2 de ancho y 0.5 de alto. Hagámoslo con el área de la base. ¿Cuál es la base, 4 × 2?
El área de la base es B = 8. Imagina esa base apoyada en la mesa — esa es una capa.
Ahora apila la base a lo alto: V = B × h = 8 × 0.5 (eso significa la mitad de 8). ¿Cuál es el volumen?
Sí, V = 4 unidades cúbicas. Compruébalo del otro modo: 4 × 2 × 0.5 = 4. La misma respuesta, porque B × h ya usó el largo y el ancho.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a rectangular prism. Formula: V = Bh = l × w × h.
vocabulary.example: V = Bh = l × w × h

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a solid shape.
vocabulary.example: A box 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³ — it holds 3 cubic feet of stuff

vocabulary.definition: A solid box shape with six flat rectangle sides.
vocabulary.example: A tissue box, a fish tank, a brick — all rectangular prisms

vocabulary.definition: The units used to measure space inside, like cubic inches.
vocabulary.example: 1 ft³ = a cube that is 1 foot on every edge

vocabulary.definition: How long, how wide, and how tall a shape is.
vocabulary.example: A box with dimensions 4 × 3 × 2 means l = 4, w = 3, h = 2

vocabulary.definition: The area of the bottom of a solid. Volume = base area × height.
vocabulary.example: If the base is 6 × 4 = 24 cm² and h = 3, then V = 24 × 3 = 72 cm³

support.prompt: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle? Use the given heights; nonsquare heights are rounded, so their areas are estimates.
support.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
feedback: 11.2 comes from adding 6 + 5.2. Area means multiply base × height, then take half.
The number is right, but ft measures length. Area needs square units (sq ft).
31.2 is 6 × 5.2 — the full rectangle. One triangle is half of that: multiply by ½.
hints: Focus on just ONE of the 6 triangles: its base is 6 ft and its height is 5.2 ft.
One triangle uses A = ½ × b × h — don't multiply by 6 yet; that step is for the whole hexagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5.2: take half of 6 first, then multiply by 5.2. Label it in sq ft.

support.prompt: A regular hexagonal skylight has 6 central triangles, each with base 6 ft and rounded height 5.2 ft. Using those measurements, what is the approximate total area?
support.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.
feedback: That is the area of ONE of the congruent triangles. The hexagon is made of 6 of them — how many triangle areas do you still need to add?
That is 4 triangles, not 6. Re-count how many congruent triangles the hexagon breaks into.
You multiplied by 12 instead of 6. Count the congruent triangles the hexagon decomposes into before you multiply.
hints: Find one central triangle’s area: ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 sq ft using the rounded height.
A regular hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles, so the total is 6 copies of one triangle's area.
Multiply 15.6 × 6. (Tip: do 15 × 6, then 0.6 × 6, and combine.)

support.prompt: A regular hexagon is split into 6 triangles, each with base 4 cm and height 3.5 cm. What is the total area? Use the given heights; nonsquare heights are rounded, so their areas are estimates.
support.explanation: Each triangle: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 sq cm. Total: 6 × 7 = 42 sq cm.
feedback: Sum for the composite area.
Identify all simple shapes.
Use the right formula for each.
hints: Two stages hide here: first one triangle (base 4 cm, height 3.5 cm), then all 6 of them.
Use ½ × 4 × 3.5 for one triangle, then multiply that result by 6 for the hexagon.
Compute ½ × 4 = 2, then 2 × 3.5 for one triangle. Now scale up by the 6 triangles.

support.prompt: How many triangles can you make from the center of a regular pentagon?
support.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so drawing lines from the center to each vertex creates 5 equal triangles.
feedback: A pentagon has 5 sides — one triangle forms per side.
Count the pentagon's sides again — one triangle each.
Too many — one triangle per side, and a pentagon has 5.
hints: 'Penta' is a clue about how many sides a pentagon has.
Drawing from the center to each corner makes exactly one triangle per side of the polygon.
Count the pentagon's sides — that count equals the number of triangles.

support.prompt: Spot the Common Mistake (use rounded heights)
steps: Decompose the octagon: A regular octagon = 8 congruent triangles
Identify one triangle: base = 3 ft, height = 4 ft
Find the area of one triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft
Find total area: Total area = 5 × 6 = 30 sq ft
support.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, not 5. Total area = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft — multiply one triangle's area by the actual number of sides (triangles), not a random number.
hints: Look at Step 4. How many sides does an octagon actually have?
An octagon has 8 sides, so it has 8 triangles: Total = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft, not 5 × 6.

support.prompt: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
support.explanation: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 cubic inches.
feedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
Not quite. V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = ___ cubic inches.
Check the units. Area is square units (²), volume is cubic units (³).
hints: Spot the three edges: l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in. Volume fills the whole box, so all three matter.
Use V = l × w × h and remember the answer needs cubic units (in³), not square units.
Multiply 4 × 3 = 12 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 5 inches.

support.prompt: A box has a volume of 36 cm³. Its length is 6 cm and width is 3 cm. What is the height?
feedback: That's the width from the problem, not the height — divide the volume by length × width instead.
That number is the length given in the problem — divide volume by the full base area to find height.
Check your division — find the full base area (length × width) before dividing into the volume.
hints: You're given the volume (36 cm³) plus two edges (6 cm and 3 cm). The height is what's missing.
Work backward: divide the volume by the base area (length × width) to uncover the height.
Find the base area first: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Then ask what number times 18 gives 36.

support.prompt: How is volume different from area?
choices: Volume measures 3D space (cubic units); area measures 2D surface (square units)
Volume uses square units; area uses cubic units
Volume only applies to cubes; area applies to all shapes
support.explanation: Volume measures the space inside a 3D shape (cubic units like in³). Area measures a flat 2D surface (square units like in²).
feedback: The units are swapped here — think about which measurement fills 3D space and which covers a flat surface.
Volume isn't just for cubes — it applies to any 3D shape, like prisms and pyramids too.
These two measurements are different — one covers a flat surface, and one fills a 3D space.
hints: Think dimensions: area covers a flat 2D surface, while volume fills a 3D space.
Match each measurement to its unit: flat surfaces get square units (²), filled space gets cubic units (³).
Picture a rug (flat) versus a fish tank (filled). Decide which is area and which is volume, then check each choice.

steps: Dimensions: A box is 5 in long, 4 in wide, and 2 in tall.
Formula: V = length × width × height
Calculate: V = 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 cubic in
Answer: Volume = 11 cubic in
support.explanation: The student added the dimensions instead of multiplying. Volume means multiply: V = 5 × 4 × 2 = 20 × 2 = 40 cubic in.
hints: Check Step 3: should you add the dimensions or multiply them?
Volume is length × width × height. Multiply: 5 × 4 × 2 = 40 cubic in, not 11.

core.prompt: Spot the Common Mistake (use rounded heights)
steps: Decompose the pentagon: A regular pentagon = 5 congruent triangles
Identify one triangle: base = 6 ft, height = 4 ft
Find the area of one triangle: A = 6 × 4 = 24 sq ft
Find total area: Total area = 5 × 24 = 120 sq ft
core.explanation: The student forgot to multiply by ½ when finding the triangle's area. A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so Total = 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
hints: Look at Step 3. What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, not just base × height. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so the total is 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.

core.prompt: Two boxes: Box A is 10 × 5 × 4 inches. Box B is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Which has more volume and by how much?
core.explanation: Box A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Box B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Box B is bigger by 40 in³.
feedback: Recheck which box's volume is larger — recalculate both totals before comparing.
You picked the right box, but recheck the subtraction to find the exact difference.
These two volumes aren't equal — calculate each box's volume and compare the totals.
hints: This asks two things: which box holds more AND by how many cubic inches — so find both volumes first.
Compute each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger.
Box A: 10 × 5 = 50, then × 4. Box B: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Compare the two totals.

core.prompt: What is the volume of a prism with edge lengths 1/2 m, 3 m, and 4 m?
feedback: That's just one edge length — volume needs all three dimensions multiplied together.
Adding the three edge lengths together won't give volume — multiply them instead.
Check the fractional edge — make sure you multiply by 1/2, not treat it as a whole number.
hints: One edge is a fraction: 1/2 m. The other edges are 3 m and 4 m. The formula works the same with fractions.
Multiply all three edges: V = 1/2 × 3 × 4. Multiplying by 1/2 is the same as dividing by 2.
Multiply the whole numbers first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then take half of that result.

core.prompt: A cube has an edge length of 5 cm. What is its volume?
core.explanation: A cube's volume is edge³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
feedback: Adding the edge three times won't give volume — multiply the edge by itself three times instead.
You squared the edge but forgot to multiply by it once more — a cube's volume needs edge × edge × edge.
Check your last multiplication — multiply the squared edge by the same edge length again.
hints: A cube's edges are all equal, so its length, width, and height are each 5 cm.
Use V = edge × edge × edge — multiply 5 by itself three times, not 5 × 3.
Start with 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply that result by 5 one more time.

Answer: Volume = 24 cubic in

stretch.prompt: Find the Area Error (use rounded heights)
steps: Decompose the hexagon: A regular hexagon = 6 triangles
Find area of one triangle: b = 5 m, h = 4.3 m
Calculate one triangle: A = ½ × 5 × 4.3 = 10.75 sq m
Find total area: Total = 10.75 + 6 = 16.75 sq m
stretch.explanation: To find total area, multiply (not add): Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m. Six equal triangles means 6 times one triangle's area.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should you use to combine 6 equal triangles?
The student added 10.75 + 6 instead of multiplying 10.75 × 6.

stretch.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon are each divided into congruent central triangles. In both polygons, each central triangle has area 15 sq ft. Which polygon has greater total area? Explain why the triangle count matters. The two polygons have different side lengths.
stretch.frame: Each triangle has area ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles, so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles, so its area is ___. Therefore ___ .
stretch.explanation: The hexagon has area 6 × 15 = 90 sq ft. The pentagon has area 5 × 15 = 75 sq ft. The hexagon has 15 sq ft more because it has one additional triangle of that area. Equal triangle areas do not require equal bases and heights.
hints: Each central triangle has the same AREA, but the triangles need not have the same shape.
A hexagon has 6 central triangles; a pentagon has 5.
Compare 6 × 15 with 5 × 15.

stretch.prompt: A fish tank measures 2 1/2 ft by 2 ft by 3 ft. What is its volume?
feedback: You multiplied two dimensions but left out the third edge length.

hints: One dimension is a mixed number: 2 1/2 ft. Rewrite it as 2.5 before multiplying.
Use V = l × w × h with all three numbers: 2.5 × 2 × 3. Keep the half — don't round it away.

stretch.prompt: A prism with a 3/4 ft by 2 ft base has a volume of 9 ft³. What is its height?
feedback: Recalculate the base area first (3/4 × 2), then divide the volume by that.
That's the volume given, not the height — divide it by the base area to find height.
Make sure you find the full base area — multiply both base dimensions before dividing.
hints: You know the volume (9 ft³) and the base dimensions (3/4 ft and 2 ft). The height is missing.
Height = Volume ÷ base area. Find the base area first, then divide the volume by it.
Base area: 3/4 × 2 = 1.5 ft². Now ask what number times 1.5 equals 9.

stretch.prompt: A toy company ships action figures in boxes that are 4 × 3 × 6 inches. A shipping crate is 24 × 12 × 18 inches. How many action figure boxes fit in the crate? Explain your reasoning step by step.
stretch.frame: Each toy box has a volume of ___ in³. The crate has a volume of ___ in³. I can fit ___ boxes because ___. I checked by ___.
stretch.explanation: Each toy box holds 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ and the crate holds 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, so 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 boxes fit. The division comes out exact because every crate edge is a whole-number multiple of a box edge: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 across, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 deep, and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 layers, and 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 confirms it.
hints: Two sizes matter: each toy box is 4 × 3 × 6 in and the crate is 24 × 12 × 18 in. Each crate edge is a multiple of a box edge.
Find both volumes, then divide the crate's volume by one box's volume. Check by counting rows, columns, and layers.
Start with one toy box: multiply 4 × 3 = 12, then multiply by 6. Next find the crate's volume the same way.
